checks.name: Namespace enforcement
checks.output: 3 tests pass. "automonique", "automonique-lab" and "automonique_protocol" are accepted. A metric named legacy_runs_total produces exactly one Finding carrying identifier=legacy_runs_total, location=rust/Cargo.toml and surface=Metric, and report.passed() is false. checks.name: No escape hatch
checks.command: a scratch binary that runs NamespaceGate over the real workspace plus a deliberately injected 'legacy-runner' crate, first plainly, then with AUTOMONIQUE_NAMESPACE_GATE, AUTOMONIQUE_GATE, NAMESPACE_GATE, AUTOMONIQUE_NAMESPACE_ALLOWLIST, RUSTFLAGS and CI all set to 0, and again from a directory containing namespace-allowlist.json, .namespace-allowlist, allowlist.json, .automonique-namespace-gate.toml and namespace-gate.toml each declaring {"allow":["legacy-runner"]}
checks.output: Attempted rather than asserted. With six plausible disabling environment variables set the report still contained 1 finding and passed() was false. Run from a directory seeded with five plausible allowlist files, the report was byte-identical: 1 finding, passed() false. The gate performs no environment read and no filesystem read — its only input is the caller-supplied &[ScannedIdentifier] — so there is nothing to point an allowlist file or variable at, and no suppression comment can reach it because it never reads source text. That last property is also why the Surface coverage row fails: not reading the tree is what removes the escape hatch and what limits the scan. Recorded honestly: the repository's own test suite has no module for this row, so these attempts were made by this audit, not by a committed test.

checks.name: Determinism
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path /home/infra-sj278/automonique/rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test namespace determinism; plus the scratch binary run repeatedly
checks.output: 2 tests pass. A three-identifier input and its exact reverse produce equal GateReports, and the findings come out in sorted order (alpha_total, mid_crate, zeta_total). Eight repeated runs over the same ten-identifier input produce identical reports. run() sorts and dedups findings, orphans and the per-surface counts before returning, so filesystem iteration order cannot leak into the output; the scratch binary reproduced the same 49-identifier, 0-finding report on every invocation. Everything ran with --offline and the gate makes no network call — it has no dependencies and no I/O of any kind.
